market_holds: Spot 49.94 at 18:17 UTC on 11-25, 0.16% above the 52-week low and 52% below the high; -7.4% over 5 sessions and -17.1% over 20 (sealed baseline). There is no usable option chain (ATM spread 112% of mid) and no sealed reaction history, so the baseline gives no implied move. Consensus is the Bloomberg Q3 net income of ARS 219.5bn, as quoted by iProfesional on 2026-11-13 and therefore 12 days old. Q2 was ARS 206.8bn, so the consensus is roughly flat in real terms. Citi is below it at 188.5bn, and Goldman expects recurring profit down 19% real with NIM falling from 17.6% to 16.3% and an ROE of 11.2%. The 2026 guide is an adjusted ROE of about 12%, with real loan growth cut to 2-5%. A buyback approved 2026-10-29 (up to ARS 160bn over 45 days, max ARS 10,700 a share) is still inside its window. The price is being set by macro rather than by the bank: country risk is 1,121bp, up from 402bp in July. Today, 11-25, a US tariff announcement, a Nasdaq drop of more than 3% and INDEC confirming a technical recession sent the Merval down about 5% and the bank ADRs down 1% to 11% (BBAR worst). The peers already out each beat consensus or EPS with lower provisions but much tighter margins: Galicia margin 17.9% to 14.4%, profit -16% QoQ; Supervielle NIM 20.3% to 16%, 2026 targets cut, ADR down about 4% on the day.
view: This print is decided by two things, and I can only see one of them. The bank itself will probably look like its peers: profit down in real terms on NIM compression, offset by lower provisions and better retail asset quality, near the 12-day-old consensus. Macro has beaten for several quarters in a row (Q2 EPS 2.17 against 1.59 expected, per Benzinga) and has the strongest capital of the group. The risk is a cut to the 2026 ROE guide like Supervielle's, and the peers' margin compression ran deeper than the Goldman-style previews. But the scored window is today's close to the 11-27 open. Between those, Argentina trades a full session on 11-26 while the US is shut for Thanksgiving, with a peso Treasury rollover of about ARS 25 trillion, country risk at a new high, the peso through 1,600 and reserves under USD 49bn. The ADR opens on the 27th at the local price times the CCL rate, so that session and the global tone are likely to swamp a consensus-sized earnings surprise. Some things push up: the stock is oversold at a 52-week low, the buyback is live in the local market, and the bank tends to beat. Some push down: macro momentum, a tight-margin quarter, a possible guide cut, and the peer pattern of beats that were still sold. I cannot tell which side wins.

recommendation.reason: I found no dated evidence of an earnings gap that the price misses and that this release would reveal inside the window. The peers' margin squeeze and provision relief are public, and the previews already carry them. The window also includes a full Argentine session on 11-26 under a live country-risk sell-off, and that session will dominate the 11-27 open.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A clear beat with the ~12% adjusted ROE guide held or raised, together with a calm 11-26 local session (Treasury rollover cleared, country risk easing), would argue long. A guide cut like Supervielle's would argue short.

self_critique: The case for long: the stock is at a 52-week low after a 17% slide that is macro rather than bank-specific; the bank is the sector's top pick at Citi, Goldman and UBS; it has beaten repeatedly; and a buyback supports the local line on 11-26. A solid print could therefore trigger a relief bounce. The case for short: macro momentum is strongly negative, a Fed-hike scare and tariffs threaten EM, and the peers' beats were sold. Neither case has evidence that is dated and specific to this window, so 50 stands.
approach_notes: P6 (find the line and the window) helped most: it showed that the 11-27 open sits behind a full Argentine session on Thanksgiving, which swamps the print. P3's peer read was useful but cannot decide a macro-dominated window. The baseline was thin (no chain, no history), so market_holds had to be rebuilt from the press.
